topic.title: What if Mexico and Spain swapped places?
topic.map_answer: Mexico's own outline laid on Spain at true scale: it covers almost all of Spain and most of Portugal, then reaches across the Mediterranean onto Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia; Spain dropped into Mexico sits almost wholly inside it

title: Drop Mexico on Spain and it won't stop at Spain
description:
Lay Mexico on Spain at its true size: where does it end?
Mexico and Spain lifted onto each other's place at true scale, and their people compared.
Sources: World Bank (Dec 2025). The characters are not advisers.
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
cta: Bigger Spain or smaller Mexico: which map would you pick? Comment

lines.text: Drop Mexico onto Spain at its real size, and it doesn't stop at Spain's coast.
Mexico has 3.9× as much land as Spain, from northern desert to southern jungle.
Spain once ruled Mexico as New Spain, from a whole ocean away.
Today the two still share a language, from Mexico City to Madrid, with an ocean in between.
Spain itself runs from the Pyrenees down to Gibraltar, with Portugal along its western side.
Lay Mexico on top, and it covers almost all of Spain, then most of Portugal next door.
Its north-west corner, Baja California, hangs out over the Atlantic beyond Portugal.
Turn it round: Spain dropped into Mexico sits almost wholly inside it, with Madrid right in the middle.
And people? For all that extra land, Mexico has only 2.7× as many as Spain.
So Spain is the more crowded one, with more people packed onto every bit of its land than Mexico.
But what about the rest of Mexico, laid on Spain: where does it end up?
Across the Mediterranean Sea and onto another continent, Africa: over Morocco, Algeria and even Tunisia.
Bigger Spain or smaller Mexico: which map would you pick? Either way, drop Mexico on Spain and it just won't stop.

[script] Payoff given away 25 s early (lesson 6, check 11): the cover beat (25.0 s) and baja beat (30.0 s) frame Mexico's whole outline on Iberia with its red south-east tail already lying over Algeria/Tunisia, so on mute the answer is on screen while the line talks about Spain and Portugal; the turn beat (50.0 s) then asks 'where does it end up?' over the same visible tail. Director: in cover/baja keep the camera on Iberia and the Atlantic (tail off frame or not yet laid), and let the tail first reach Africa on the payoff's 'Mediterranean'/'Africa'.

[script] Same picture two beats in a row (check D): cover (25.0 s) and baja (30.0 s) are the same overlay at nearly the same framing, only a BAJA CALIFORNIA label added; turn (50.0 s) repeats it again. Give baja its own shot (close on the Baja arm over the sea off Portugal, waves under it) and turn a different angle.

[script] 10.0 s (size beat): the four stacked Spain shapes overlap each other and the Pacific edge of Mexico in a pile, so '3.9x' doesn't read as a count of Spains; lay them side by side (or inside Mexico) without overlap. Also the ratio sign rises on 'land', after '3.9x' is spoken (5.0 s still has no sign) - have it up on the figure's word; the line is 19 words / 5.1 s, over lesson 1's ~15 words / 5 s.

[script] 55.0 s (payoff): MEDITERRANEAN is written on the overlay over Spain's land, not on the sea, and Morocco's red highlight is the same red as Mexico's flag stripe beside it, so which shape is which is hard to read; put the label on open water and light Morocco/Algeria in a colour distinct from the flag.
